question.problem:
Compute the gradient of the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R$ defined by $$ f(x)={x}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]x $$ with respect to $x$ at $x={[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{T}.$
$\,{∇}_{x}f=\,\,$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
Defining the matrix $A$ as

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we have $f(x)={x}^{T}Ax.$

Since $A$ is not symmetric, we use the more general formula for the gradient of a quadratic function:

$$
{∇}_{x}f(x)=({A}^{T}+A)x
$$

First, we compute

$$
{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}+A & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, compute the gradient at $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x}f(x) & =({A}^{T}+A)x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4-3 \\ 3+4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
